answer: Memory-hard registration puzzle: to join or renew each epoch, an identity must solve a fresh Argon2 puzzle tied to a random seed and its own key, sized to need gigabytes of RAM for minutes. Any verifier rechecks the solution in milliseconds. Each extra identity costs its own RAM-minutes, so splitting one operator into many multiplies hardware and power bills; a cool tundra data center gives no oasis of free compute. Limits: a large farm pays a lower per-unit price, and each epoch's cost spike sends a ripple of exclusion through agents on small machines.
